Pt(553) electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: Bead-type Pt(553) electrodes were prepared following the Clavilier method before every experiment; the electrode was flame annealed for 1 min, allowed to cool in an Ar/H2 (3:1) atmosphere and then dipped into ultrapure water saturated with the same gas mixture. Transfer through air to the electrochemical cell occurred while the surface of the electrode was protected with a droplet of water.
nodes.source_text: Bead-type Pt(111) and Pt(553) electrodes were prepared following the Clavilier method37 before every experiment; the electrode was flame annealed for 1 min...

nodes.name: Step decoration with metal adatoms
nodes.procedure: Metal adatoms were deposited selectively at the Pt step edge by cycling the Pt(553) electrode from 0.06 to 0.35 V_RHE for 10–100 cycles in 0.1 M HClO4 that contained 10^{-5} to 10^{-6} M metal cation (Mo^{x+}, Re^{7+}, Ru^{3+}, Rh^{3+}, Ag^{+}). Similar procedures were used previously to deposit Ru and Ag onto stepped platinum. The concentration and number of cycles were varied to control the amount of metal atom deposited at the step. For Ru example: cycling in 1 M HClO4 + 10^{-6} M RuCl3.

nodes.name: Ru*-decorated Pt(553)
aliases: Pt(553) with Ru* at the step edge

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammogram in 0.1 M HClO4 shows three features: hydrogen adsorption on (111)-like terrace sites (0.06-0.3 V_RHE), H/OH/H2O exchange at (110) step edge (0.125 V_RHE), and hydroxide adsorption on terrace (0.6-0.85 V_RHE). After Ru decoration, the step edge peak at 0.125 V_RHE is eliminated while terrace hydrogen adsorption is unaffected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CV in 0.1 M HClO4 in Fig. 1b shows three features: a broad peak due to hydrogen adsorption on (111)-like terrace sites (0.06−0.3 VRHE), a sharp peak due to an exchange between hydrogen and co-adsorbed hydroxide and water at the (110) step edge (0.125 VRHE) ... and a peak at high potentials due to the adsorption of hydroxide on the (111)-like terrace (0.6−0.85 VRHE).

nodes.characterization_summary: After Ru* deposition, the sharp peak at 0.125 V_RHE due to H/OH/H2O exchange at Pt step edge is eliminated, confirming selective step decoration, while hydrogen adsorption on terrace remains unaffected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The voltammogram measured after the deposition of Ru shows that the Ru* blocks the adsorption of the hydrogen and hydroxide at the Pt step edge, which eliminates the sharp peak at 0.125 VRHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER activity (current density at -0.038 V_RHE) on Ru*-decorated Pt(553) shows linear relationship with Ru* coverage (R²=0.98), reaching 65 times higher activity than bare Pt(553) at 1 ML coverage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d gives the rate of the HER on the Ru-decorated Pt(553) as a function of Ru* coverage. ... The activity of the Ru*-decorated step edge, extrapolated to a complete 1 monolayer (ML, defined per step Pt atom) coverage, is 65 times that of the bare Pt(553) surface.

visual_evidence.name: Current Density vs Ru Coverage Plot

properties.y_axis: Current density (mA cm⁻² at 0.38 V vs RHE)

nodes.characterization_summary: Polarization curves measured at similar high adatom coverages show HER rates (ln j at -0.038 V_RHE, iR-corrected) follow volcano relationship with DFT-calculated OH* adsorption free energy at 0 V_RHE for bare and Mo*, Re*, Ru*, Rh*, Ag*-decorated Pt(553) step edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 illustrates that the experimentally measured rate of the HER in an alkaline electrolyte follows a volcano type relationship with the DFT-calculated binding strength of hydroxide on the adatom at the step. The HER activity is measured at similar adatom coverages, given in Supplementary Table 1.

properties.y_label: log(|j_MA| / mA cm⁻²) at V_RHE = 0.98 V

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations show negligible effect of Re*, Ru*, Rh* at Pt(553) step on hydrogen binding strength to terrace sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations support that the presence of Re, Ru and Rh at the step have only a small or negligible effect on the binding strength of hydrogen to the terrace (Supplementary Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT activation energies for water dissociation (to adsorbed OH* and to solution-phase OH-) at 0 V_RHE show linear Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi relationship (slope 0.27) with OH* adsorption free energy for bare Pt(553), Pt(111), and Re*, Ru*, Rh*, Ag*-decorated Pt(553) step edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows how the activation energy for water dissociation is linearly correlated with the binding strength of the adsorbed hydroxide at the step edge (and on Pt(111), included for comparison).
